---
title: "Estimates and sampling error"
subtitle: "1.2 · one simulated unit, after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024) and Walters' teaching slides"
description: "Sampling variation of a normally distributed estimate with a fixed true value and known standard error."
---

Repeated samples add fresh random noise of standard deviation SE to a fixed true value, placing about two-thirds of estimates within one SE.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **SE .20.** Across 20 estimates of true value .50, 12 of 20 fall within one SE (vs. 13.7 expected); draw 20 gives .229 (.50 plus noise −.271).
- **200 draws.** Over 200 draws, 132 of 200 fall within one SE against 137 expected (expected share .683).
- **Seed 2.** A second sample places 18 of 20 estimates within one SE against the same 13.7 expected average.
- **SE .10.** Halving the SE shrinks the noise arrow to −.136 while preserving standardized noise (−1.36 SEs) and 12 of 20 within one SE.
- **SE .05.** Halving the SE again shrinks noise to −.0678 and keeps 12 of 20 within one SE.

Source: Simulated normal estimate-plus-noise model after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024, Section III, Assumption 1; talk slide 17), Walters (Mixtape slides, pp. 5–6), and postrank theory book, ch. 2.
